title: Every translation passes a layered fidelity check and a reader of its language
description:
As an editor, I want each localization version checked against the exact original version it came from and reviewed by a person who reads that language, so translated pages keep the reporting's facts, certainty and quotations.

Layers: deterministic (numbers, dates, units, URLs, citation anchors, quotation count, Markus structure, glossary and do-not-translate names; language-aware, since fact_check.py is English-only today), a bilingual model judge block by block (meaning, certainty, omissions, additions), Humanus checks with target-language policies, and a language reviewer step on the localization's checklist drawn from a translation procedure template. A language with no reviewer stays preview-only. Plan: docs/plans/multilingual-publishing.md (PR #1450).

Feature: Checking translations

Scenario: A changed figure is caught
  Given an English paragraph says 40 percent
  When its Spanish translation says 14 por ciento
  Then the fidelity check reports the number mismatch against the English version

Scenario: Softened or hardened certainty is caught
  Given an English sentence says a policy may change
  When its translation says the policy will change
  Then the model judge reports changed certainty for that block

Scenario: No reviewer, no public language
  Given no person who reads Chinese is assigned to the site
  When an editor tries to close the language review step of a Chinese localization
  Then the step cannot be closed and the language stays in preview
